 PA health insurance open enrollment is underway. Key Pennie deadlines
 Damon C. Williams, USA Today Network 2026년 11월 9일 월 오후 2:55 UTC 0 Pennsylvania's health insurance marketplace is open for 2027 enrollment, giving state residents who buy their own coverage a chance to shop for a new plan or review the one they already have.
 Open enrollment through Pennie began Nov. 1 and continues through Jan. 15, 2027. Pennsylvanians who want new coverage to begin Jan. 1 need to enroll by Dec. 15. 
 Here's what Pennsylvania residents need to know about the deadlines, costs and decisions ahead.
 When is Pennie open enrollment for 2027?
 Pennie is Pennsylvania's official health insurance marketplace for individuals and families who don't have another coverage option, such as insurance through an employer.
 Pennie open enrollment runs through Jan. 15. The most immediate date to remember, however, is Dec. 15. You will need to enroll by then to have new coverage beginning Jan. 1.
 Outside the annual enrollment window, people generally need a qualifying life event, such as losing existing health coverage, getting married or moving, to qualify for a special enrollment period. 
 Advertisement
 How much could Pennie health insurance cost in 2027?
 Many Pennsylvania households could be paying more for Pennie health insurance in 2027.
 The Pennsylvania Insurance Department approved an average 15.97% increase in 2027 premiums for Pennsylvania's individual health insurance market. That doesn't mean every Pennie customer's bill will rise by 15.97%; actual costs depend on the plan selected and any financial assistance a household qualifies to receive.
 Financial help remains important. Pennie says four out of five enrollees qualify for financial savings, and Pennie is the only marketplace where Pennsylvanians can apply for federal tax credits that lower premiums and out-of-pocket costs. 
 Those costs and savings can change from year to year, making this an especially important enrollment period for comparison shopping.
 Damon C. Williams is a Philadelphia-based journalist reporting on trending, breaking and service-related topics across the Mid-Atlantic region for the USA Today Network.
